correspondence.component_scope: headward-feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in western Villa Pesqueira municipality, west/northwest of the town, on a tributary corridor north of Presa La Hacienda. The SGM original depicts the west/southwest watercourse and its western valley junction; the municipal map independently supplies the generalized headward setting. The selected opening is not treated as a passage through that reservoir, and no whole-opening hydronym is assigned from nearby labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: mazatan-valley
correspondence.finding: The route turns south along the eastern foot of the Sierra de Mazatán, passes the Mazatán town setting and receives the separately mapped eastward tributary approaches. The municipal original explicitly labels the matched south-running reach Río Mazatán. Its continuation toward the southwest is followed across the municipal edge; no exact name-change vertex is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: matape-middle-corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest main-valley course corresponds to the river labeled Río Matape in the La Colorada original. Tributary junctions, the El Garambullo approach and the San José de Pimas setting distinguish it from neighboring La Poza and Tecoripa drainage. This is channel-and-junction correspondence, not only basin association.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: matape-southeast-bend
correspondence.finding: The original maps carry the main river through its southeastward bend, then south into the northern Guaymas corridor. Overlapping cartography establishes the intervening connector rather than assuming it from model connectivity.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: alatorre-reservoir-connector
correspondence.finding: The mapped Río Mátape approach continues into the Presa Ignacio R. Alatorre setting and emerges toward the southwest as the mapped Río San Marcial. The original shows the through-going reservoir/outlet relationship and nearby lateral drainage. This component contains river and reservoir settings, so it receives no single local scalar name. Exact reservoir-shore and hydronym-transition points are not claimed.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: san-marcial-lower-valley
correspondence.finding: Below the reservoir the selected long southwest course follows Río San Marcial, then turns south along the eastern side of Sierra Santa Úrsula toward northern Empalme. The Guaymas map preserves the major lateral tributary setting; the Empalme original supplies the continuing lower course.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: empalme-terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final course follows the curving western San Marcial drainage past the northern Empalme agricultural plain to the coastal embayment immediately north/northwest of Empalme, in the Gulf of California setting. The original maps distinguish the straight irrigation canals and easterly coastal drains. The terminal is the coast beyond the reservoir, not the reservoir itself. No exact mouth vertex or more specific bay-name assignment is required or asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern selected opening near Back Tuttle Spring and Pease Flat
correspondence.finding: The eastern opening is on a mapped headward drainage by Back Tuttle Spring. The selected route follows that small drainage southeast, then southwest through the Pease Flat wetland setting, where it meets the mapped Fletcher Creek network. It then continues south past the Green Spring Reservoir side approach before turning west near Mulkey Place and Grassy Ravine. The opening is not identified solely from the nearby Fletcher Creek label: the blue drainage and its downstream junction were read. No separate hydronym is established for the initial feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Fletcher Creek, Dry Valley junction setting and Boles Meadow
correspondence.finding: The westward selected course follows the mapped Fletcher Creek corridor into the Dry Valley wetland/Willow Creek junction setting, then continues south and southwest on the repeatedly labeled Fletcher Creek channel. The route passes the mapped Avanzino Reservoir setting and lower wetland reaches into Boles Meadow. The northern Willow Creek approach is separately mapped and is not substituted for the selected eastern opening. Green Spring Reservoir and the other lateral ponds are not promoted to selected lake crossings.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.name_scope: Mapped named creek reaches only; the initial feeder name and precise creek-name transition points remain unassigned.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Boles Meadow to Boles Creek and the lower Willow Creek junction
correspondence.finding: At Boles Meadow the selected route turns west and then northwest onto the mapped Boles Creek corridor. It continues north past the Mitchell Valley setting, along the same channel west of Steele Swamp, and meets Willow Creek approaching from the northeast. The map shows the selected Boles approach and the receiving Willow Creek channel as distinct named components. The long northward reach is not inferred from basin membership: its continuous channel and matching valley bends were read.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Willow Creek, eastern Clear Lake margin and Lost River outlet
correspondence.finding: From the Boles Creek junction the selected connection follows the labeled Willow Creek west around the Sagebrush Butte/Mammoth Springs setting into the eastern margin of the large lake at Clear Lake National Wildlife Refuge. The selected generalized passage turns north at that eastern marsh/lake margin into the channel labeled Lost River and continues through its outlet corridor. Reclamation independently identifies Clear Lake Dam and Reservoir on Lost River; this supports the reservoir identity alongside the cartographic placement and connected outlet. The model follows the eastern connecting margin rather than traversing both lake lobes. River/creek labels extending into open water on the composite map are not treated as uniform hydronyms for the reservoir.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original Boles/Clear and Clear/Bonanza map pixels; bounded Reclamation facilities prose identifying the reservoir and river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lost River below Clear Lake, Rock Creek junction, Malone and state-line turn
correspondence.finding: Below the Clear Lake outlet the selected river follows the mapped Lost River canyon northwest past Elder Spring and Plum Spring, the Rock Creek side junction, Carr Butte and the Cape Home setting. It reaches the Malone Pool/Walte Flat interval, receives the separately mapped East Branch Lost River from the Willow Valley Reservoir direction, and bends north across the California–Oregon boundary into Langell Valley. The East Branch/Willow Valley Reservoir branch is lateral, not part of the selected main course. Reclamation identifies Malone Diversion Dam on Lost River downstream of Clear Lake.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Langell Valley, Miller Creek junction and Bonanza
correspondence.finding: The selected northward line corresponds to the straightened Lost River corridor through lower Langell Valley and its wetland/agricultural floor. It continues northwest past the Miller Creek approach from the east, through the Lorella-area valley and then north and west to Bonanza. The map also shows Miller Creek upstream toward Gerber Reservoir; that reservoir branch is outside the selected route. The continuous selected corridor, major junction and Bonanza bend are covered by the overlapping cartographic views.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Bonanza through Poe Valley, Olene and Lost River Pool
correspondence.finding: At Bonanza the mapped Lost River turns west and southwest, past the Buck Creek and Wright Creek side approaches, then follows the broad Poe Valley corridor westward. The selected route rounds the same valley bends before passing through The Gap at Olene and the widened Lost River Pool reach southwest of Olene. Nearby Alkali Lake, Nuss Lake and the B/C canals are separately depicted; their labels and paths are not transferred to the selected river.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Lost River Diversion Channel junction and lower river to Merrill
correspondence.finding: The mapped Lost River continues from the pool to the Lost River Diversion Channel junction. The selected route turns south on Lost River rather than west along the diversion channel. It follows the river around the foot of Modoc Ridge through the Merrill Division area, passing the adjacent C Canal and agricultural drains before reaching Merrill. Reclamation explains that the diversion dam can send excess water toward the Klamath River; that engineered branch does not change which route this selection follows.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Merrill, lower impounded river and Hatfield–Tulelake approach
correspondence.finding: At Merrill the selected course turns east and southeast along the mapped broad Lost River bends and the Malone Road/J Canal junction setting. It then follows the river southeast through Hatfield across the state boundary, and south beside the agricultural grid west of the City of Tulelake to the northern Tule Lake margin. Reclamation places Anderson-Rose Diversion Dam on this lower Lost River reach and describes the reclaimed lakebed it serves. The river-to-lake entry is visible, not inferred from the nearby refuge label.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Tule Lake entry, internal wetland/waterbody passage and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The northern approach enters the mapped Tule Lake marsh and open-water complex within the dyked lake/refuge setting. The final straight selected extension continues south within the marsh/open-water body and ends inside the area repeatedly labeled Tule Lake. It is an internal modeled lake passage, not a separately named river channel or an outlet to the ocean. Reclamation documents controlled flow into the Tule Lake sumps and a pumped tunnel connection toward Lower Klamath; those managed connections are outside this selected terminal extension. Ordinary lake-setting correspondence is complete without requiring a precise contemporary shoreline or mouth point.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_component_corridor_scale
correspondence.reading_scope: Original bounded USGSTopo raster pixels and private enlargement/orientation crops.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and first northeastern bend
correspondence.finding: The western/southern opening and its first northward and northeastern bend are within the continuous southeastern Inland Ice, well west of the exposed Umivik coastal rocks. The original graticule and ice-surface contours cover the full opening.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The map depicts an ice-covered setting rather than a named river channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward corridor and small southeastward steps
correspondence.finding: The upper eastward sequence and its small southward steps remain within continuous mapped ice. There is no intervening exposed coastal belt, mapped through-lake or reservoir passage requiring a separate source connector.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Absence of a depicted lake passage is a bounded map observation, not an assertion about all supraglacial or subglacial water bodies.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern middle excursion and long northern eastward segment
correspondence.finding: The northeastward leg and long northern eastward sequence lie on the ice-covered interior immediately inland of the southeast coast. The original map supplies continuous coverage across the bend and the entire eastward segment. Blue surface contours and dashed ice-thickness lines are identified by the original legend as ice information.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Ice contours and aeromagnetic lineaments must not be interpreted as river traces.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward descent and lower eastward approach
correspondence.finding: The southeastern descent and successive eastward steps approach the Umivik coastal ice margin. The national original continues to show the glaciated setting, with exposed coastal rocks farther east and south. The final small northeastern steps before the last southeastward turn are included in the same continuous source reading.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No mapped named-river confluence, through-lake or reservoir connector is established on the selected corridor; modeled line connectivity alone is not taken as natural-river evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southeastward turn, short eastward ending and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The actual ending belongs to the glaciated inner coastal setting west of the Umivik label. Original terminal-region pixels show the low ice-surface contour sequence meeting a rock-fringed embayment/coastal margin. This accounts for the selected marine-terminal setting at generalized scale without extending the interpretation to the offshore sea or another named fjord.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The retained model labels this terminal sea. The historical national map supports the coastal/ice-margin context, not exact agreement with a present glacier front, bank or mouth point. Umivik is not adopted as a natural-river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 11671
correspondence.finding: The selected start south of Torre do Monte Alegre runs south and west before turning north into Igarapé Zinco. Both originals depict Zinco and a separate Bom Lugar feeder; the 2010 source labels that feeder Ig. da Praça and shows it joining Zinco farther north. Neither depicts the selected southern connector, so Praça or the nearby wetland cannot close that gap. From the mapped upper Zinco reach northward, the corridor is read into Rio Anajás near Flecheira/Casinha, past São Francisco, Pedra and Alto Anajás to Anajás town and the Mocões junction. It continues northwest and north past Caruso/Boas Novas, the Aramã joining near Jurará, and Nova Filadélfia at the Guajará joining. The model stores this entire mixed-scope fragment as mainstem; that does not make Zinco or the unresolved feeder uniformly Anajás.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 11673
correspondence.finding: The lower Anajás runs west from the Cururu vicinity past Boa Vista, Patauá and Repouso, bends south through Baixo Anajás, then west past the Pau de Rosa/Porto Alegre passage. Jipuru joins from the south; the model takes the broad southern anabranch before turning north beside Japichauá/Porto Cacique and rejoining near Selvinha Batista. Parallel Breu/Acara Pereira and São João Velho/Guajará-Miri channels remain distinct. From there the selected route follows the broad northwestern Rio Anajás past Vila do Irmão Tita and the Santa Maria/Charapucu joining toward Jupati/Nazaré and Vila Monte. The selected endpoint remains within the broad channel east of Ilha das Guaribas, with continued water northward. Stored sea class is not treated as an open-ocean mouth or the ultimate river outlet.
